title: Hunkar Begendi
subtitle: Turkish lamb stew served on smoked aubergine cream
excerpt: Tender braised lamb sits on a silky aubergine puree enriched with butter and cheese. The aubergine must be charred directly over a flame to get the smoky depth this dish is built on.
sourceNotes: Ottoman palace cuisine, associated with Sultan Murad IV. The smoked aubergine cream base is the defining technique.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the lamb stew only. Make the aubergine cream fresh on the day as it does not freeze well.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb stew improves overnight. Reheat gently and make the aubergine cream just before serving.

content.text: Hunkar begendi pairs braised lamb with a smoked aubergine cream. Char the aubergines directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill until the skin is black and the flesh collapses. The smoke is not optional; it is the whole point of the dish.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Brown the lamb pieces well on all sides. Do this in batches. Set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Fry the onion in the same pan for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and paprika and cook for 1 minute more.
Return the lamb. Stir in the tomato puree, tinned tomatoes, and 200 ml of water. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60 minutes until the lamb is very tender. Stir every 15 minutes. Add a splash of water if it looks dry.

While the lamb cooks, char the aubergines. Hold them over a gas flame with tongs, turning every 2 minutes, until the skin is black and collapsed all over. This takes about 10 to 12 minutes each. Cool, then peel and squeeze out any liquid. Chop the flesh roughly.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the warm milk, stirring all the time, until you have a smooth thick sauce.
Stir the aubergine flesh and grated cheese into the sauce. Season with salt. Spoon the cream onto warm plates, top with the lamb stew, and scatter over the parsley.

items.cause: The milk was added too fast or was cold.
items.fix: Add warm milk a little at a time and whisk between each addition.

items.symptom: The cream has no smoky flavour.
items.cause: The aubergines were not charred enough.
items.fix: The skin needs to be fully black and the flesh completely soft. Keep going until you can feel the whole aubergine collapsing.

items.symptom: The lamb is tough after an hour.
items.cause: The heat was too high and the liquid evaporated.
items.fix: Add more water and continue cooking. Shoulder needs a low, steady simmer to become tender.
